newsitem.title: USA: KEDO and NKorea start financial protocol talks.
newsitem.headline: KEDO and NKorea start financial protocol talks.

text.p: North Korea and an international consortium began talks on Tuesday to establish procedures to be followed if one of the parties fails to meet its financial obligations under a 1994 agreement to change Pyongyang's nuclear programme.

Representatives of the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO) -- led by the United States, South Korea and Japan -- and North Korea posed briefly for photographers at the KEDO offices in New York before the meeting started.

Under the $4.5 billion deal, Washington promised the isolationist state two light-water reactors generating 1,000 megawatts of power each by approximately 2003 if Pyongyang would freeze and ultimately dismantle its existing nuclear programme.
North Korea was assured interim energy in the form of 500,000 metric tonnes of heavy fuel oil per year for heating and electricity.

Tuesday's talks were the start of discussions on "a protocol concerning actions in the event of nonpayment with respect to financial obligations in connection with the light-water reactor project," a KEDO statement said.
The talks will continue until agreement was reached on the protocol, essentially one that would establish what penalties would be levied for nonpayment by either side, a KEDO official said.
Five other protocols have been concluded since the 1994 supply agreement was signed.
The agreement calls for the consortium to pay for a host of tasks, from the provision of the two light-water reactor plants to site survey and preparations and nuclear fuel, among other costs.
The deal requires that KEDO will be repaid by North Korea interest-free over 20 years, including a three-year grace period, after the completion of the light-water reactors.
Light-water reactors are less suitable for producing weapons-grade plutonium than the graphite-moderated reactors built by North Korea.
